criterion_notes.c1: Examines household drinking-water and sanitation/sewerage service access, piped coverage, daily per-capita water supply sufficiency, intermittent delivery (tandeo), and household affordability across all 84 municipalities of Hidalgo, Mexico.
criterion_notes.c2: Explicit assessment under both readings: Under the plain wording of Criterion 2, the paper clearly qualifies (yes) because it examines legal, regulatory, and governance factors including constitutional Human Right to Water (Article 4) compliance, municipal and intermunicipal utility provision (Article 115, CAASIM), REPDA water concessions, and municipal tariff laws. Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism clarification, the paper also qualifies (yes) because it directly extracts and quantitatively evaluates statutory tariff rules — residential water, sewerage, and sanitation tariffs enacted in Decrees 55-170 of the 2022 Municipal Revenue, Quotas, and Tariffs Law across 84 municipalities and CAASIM intermunicipal utility tariff schedules (8 m3 minimum household block and rural/urban differentiated tariffs from 2013 to 2022) — alongside legally conceded domestic and public-urban water volumes registered in REPDA under the National Waters Law governing municipal supply availability and household affordability.
criterion_notes.c3: Quantitative descriptive empirical study analyzing secondary institutional, legal, and survey datasets across 84 municipalities of Hidalgo (REPDA 2022 water concessions, 2022 statutory municipal tariff decrees, CAASIM 2013-2022 tariffs, INEGI 2020 Census, INEGI MOHOMA 2017 bottled water expenditure, CONASAMI 2013-2022 minimum wages, and CONAGUA SINA water quality/discharge records).
criterion_notes.c4: Reports municipal- and household-level outcomes on water affordability (monthly water tariff plus bottled water expenditure as a percentage of 1- and 2-minimum-wage household income relative to the 3% HRW threshold), per-capita water supply sufficiency (liters/inhabitant/day relative to 50 L minimum and 100 L optimal thresholds), piped water and sewerage coverage (%), intermittent supply (tandeo), and water source contamination.
criterion_notes.c5: Population and units of analysis (households and all 84 municipalities in Hidalgo, Mexico, total population 3,083,841, plus 2013-2022 time series for CAASIM-served households), rule-type exposures (statutory municipal and CAASIM residential water/sewerage/sanitation tariffs and REPDA domestic/public-urban water concessions), access/affordability/sufficiency outcomes, and descriptive cross-sectional and longitudinal quantitative design are all clearly specified. Per Criterion 6, lack of an inferential regression effect estimate is a quantitative-synthesis gate rather than a review-eligibility gate.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in Spanish (with abstracts in Spanish, English, Portuguese, French, and Italian). Per Criterion 9 and Criterion 10, Spanish is eligible because translation from the provided 21-page full text is directly feasible and the study is relevant; the translation method and translator should be logged in extraction_note at data extraction.

evidence_quotes.quote: El objetivo de este trabajo fue cuantificar los niveles de asequibilidad que garantizan el Derecho Humano al Agua (DHA) en los hogares del Estado, para lo cual se estimaron proporciones de dotación de agua que arriba a los hogares, la calidad y el gasto, utilizando datos institucionales —nacionales, estatales y municipales—, incluidos los emitidos por organismos operadores de agua.
se extrajo información del Periódico Oficial del Estado de Hidalgo
La tarifa corresponde a la establecida por la CAASIM, la dotación mínima por hogar es de 8m3 e incluye los servicios de saneamiento y alcantarillado;
lo anterior con la finalidad de estimar la disponibilidad de litros diarios de agua por habitante a nivel municipal

cabe destacar que cada municipio tiene tarifas de agua diferentes, superando el 3 % del ingreso familiar, lo que hace evidente que desde esta perspectiva el DHA se está vulnerando y en gran medida deriva del gasto que se realiza por la compra de agua embotellada (Mapa 4).

raw_response.exposure: Statutory municipal residential water, sewerage, and sanitation tariffs (Ley de ingresos, cuotas y tarifas municipales 2022, Decrees 55-170) and CAASIM intermunicipal utility tariff rules (2013-2022, 8 m3 minimum block and rural/urban tariff differentiation), alongside REPDA legally conceded domestic and public-urban water volumes under the Ley de Aguas Nacionales.
raw_response.outcome: Household water affordability (total monthly expenditure on utility water/sewerage tariff plus bottled water as % of 1- and 2-minimum-wage household income vs. 3% HRW benchmark), municipal per-capita daily water availability/sufficiency (L/inhabitant/day vs. 50 L and 100 L benchmarks), piped water and sewerage coverage (%), and service continuity (tandeo).
raw_response.population_and_sample: Households and municipalities across all 84 municipalities of the State of Hidalgo, Mexico (3,083,841 inhabitants in 2020 Census; 84 municipalities analyzed cross-sectionally in 2022 and 10-year longitudinal series 2013-2022 for CAASIM-served households).
raw_response.rationale: This Spanish-language full-text empirical study satisfies all review inclusion criteria under both the plain and narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type readings of Criterion 2. Using institutional administrative and census datasets across all 84 municipalities of Hidalgo, Mexico (and a 2013-2022 series for the intermunicipal utility CAASIM), the authors extract statutory municipal water, sewerage, and sanitation tariffs enacted in Decrees 55-170 of the 2022 Municipal Revenue and Tariffs Law, CAASIM minimum-block tariff schedules, and REPDA legally conceded domestic/public-urban water volumes to quantify household water affordability (% of 1- and 2-minimum-wage income) and per-capita daily water sufficiency against constitutional Human Right to Water thresholds. Spanish full text is eligible under Criterion 10 as translation is directly feasible.
raw_response.study_design: Quantitative descriptive cross-sectional municipal analysis (84 municipalities) and longitudinal time-series analysis (2013-2022) using secondary administrative, legal-tariff, and census datasets
